lessons.title: Consolidating the full conversation loop
lessons.focus: Consolidating the full greeting-and-response conversation loop with retrieval first and no new material.
lessons.practised: Oi; Bom dia; Eu sou Dan; Como você está?; Estou bem; E você?; Estou cansado. Full exchange practised twice.
lessons.mastered: Oi, Bom dia, Eu sou Dan, the meaning of Como você está?, and production of Como você está? were recalled independently. Estou bem was not recalled independently at first and needed a model. E você? was also not recalled independently initially and needed prompting/modeling. Estou cansado was attempted independently but came out incorrectly before being corrected, then was produced successfully. In the later full exchanges, Dan responded naturally with Estou bem, e você? and Estou cansado without needing the full answer supplied. No new phrases are marked mastered.
lessons.mistakes: Retrieval of Estou bem remains weak from an English cue. E você? was still difficult to retrieve independently. Estou cansado was initially produced incorrectly as something sounding like “contrado,” then corrected quickly.
lessons.pronunciation: Como você está? was produced smoothly. Eu sou Dan was clear. Estou bem was clear once modeled. Estou cansado improved immediately after correction and was then used correctly in the exchange.
lessons.roleplay: Dan successfully completed the full opening sequence: “Oi, bom dia. Eu sou Dan. Como você está?” In the first role-play he replied with “Estou bem, e você?” and later “Estou cansado.” He repeated the full exchange a second time with good flow. The conversation loop is becoming functional, but retrieval of individual response phrases still needs checking outside the memorized sequence.
lessons.next: Start the next lesson by testing “I’m well,” “And you?” and “I’m tired” separately with no model. Then run the full exchange again. If those responses are independently recalled, begin adding one new Estou… response such as Estou animado.
lessons.notes:
Source: Dan’s supplied lesson log for 11 September 2026. This entry records the supplied observations; it is not a new audio assessment.

Comprehension: Dan independently remembered that Como você está? means “How are you?” This was stronger than the previous lesson.

Mastery: No new phrases marked mastered yet. Oi and Bom dia remain strongest. The full conversation loop is improving, but Estou bem, E você? and Estou cansado should remain Developing until they can be retrieved independently from meaning cues.

lessons.title: Greetings, introductions & responding with Estou…
lessons.focus: Greetings, introductions, asking how someone is, and responding with Estou…
lessons.practised: Oi; Bom dia; Eu sou Dan; Como você está?; Estou bem; E você?; Estou cansado. Combined into a short morning conversation.
lessons.mastered: Oi and Bom dia were recalled independently (Functional). Eu sou Dan needed prompting at first, then was produced correctly inside the full greeting. Como você está? could be pronounced after review, but its meaning was not recalled independently at first. Estou bem, E você? and Estou cansado were newly introduced, repeated and used with prompting; none is independently mastered.
lessons.mistakes: Eu sou initially sounded like “El Sou” and needed several repetitions. Estou bem was briefly confused with Estou Dan; bem needed clarification. Cansado needed a pronunciation correction. E você? was repeatedly forgotten at first, then became more comfortable.
lessons.pronunciation: Eu sou improved and was later clear inside Oi, bom dia. Eu sou Dan. Como você está? became smoother with repetition. Estou bem needed emphasis on bem. Cansado needed a brief sound correction, then improved.
lessons.roleplay: Dan produced Oi, bom dia. Eu sou Dan. Como você está? He later used Estou bem, e você? and Estou cansado, e você? with prompting. In the final longer attempt, most of the conversation was produced, but Estou cansado still needed a recall prompt.
lessons.next: Start with retrieval only, with no model first: Oi, Bom dia, Eu sou Dan, meaning and production of Como você está?, Estou bem, E você? and Estou cansado. Recheck eu sou, bem and cansado. Then run the full greeting-and-response exchange without supplying answers. Only add another Estou… response if recall is strong.
lessons.notes:
Source: the lesson handoff supplied by Dan for 9 September 2026. This is a supplied lesson log, not a reconstruction or a fresh audio assessment.

Meaning / comprehension: Como você está? (“How are you?”) was not recalled at first; understood after explanation. Estou bem = “I’m well / I’m good”; E você? = “And you?”; Estou cansado = “I’m tired.”

Strongest material: Oi, Bom dia and the full chunk Oi, bom dia. Eu sou Dan. are becoming functional. Estou bem, e você? showed good fluency after repetition, but needs retrieval testing.

Still developing: meaning and spontaneous use of Como você está?; Estou bem; E você?; Estou cansado; fully independent Eu sou Dan without a prompt.

Recommended focus: reinforce the full conversation loop until independent. Keep Estou cansado as a variation. Repetition alone does not count as mastery; do not mark the new responses mastered.
